correctness.rationale: For finite open path adjacency H with simple sine spectrum E_ℓ=2 cos(πℓ/(N+1)), protected modes vanish at every positive-rate monitored vertex iff (N+1)|ℓr for every r in S, exactly ℓ=m(N+1)/g where g=gcd(N+1,S); protected dimension g−1. The Hilbert–Schmidt dissipation identity Re⟨X,LX⟩=−(1/2)∑γ_r||[P_r,X]||² shows all imaginary-axis eigenoperators commute with each monitor. At zero frequency the ground sine mode nonzero everywhere couples all monitored-visible energy coefficients to a single bright scalar. At nonzero fixed Bohr frequency simple energies make X have at most one entry per row/column, triangular/nilpotent; [X,P_r]=0 then forces X|r⟩=0 and ⟨r|X=0, so only dark-to-dark matrix units survive. Contractivity excludes peripheral Jordan growth; finite dimensionality gives exponential decay of all other modes and the claimed operator asymptote for arbitrary initial densities. Cesàro averaging kills nonzero dark energy differences, reducing the position kernel to a finite sine-fourth-product sum. The root-of-unity cosine sum gives the displayed gcd-residue kernel with bright factor (1−w_j)(1−w_k)/(N−g+1), and reveals the g=1/g=2/g≥3 mixing trichotomy. Independently evaluated the sine product sum versus the closed formula for all sites and one-site monitor placements on N=2,...,25, checking row normalization; finite numerical checks support only the finite identity examples, not arbitrary N proof. Source verify.py contains direct small-N Liouvillian diagonalization as a separate consistency check.
